g1.flow: Al-Mursalāt asks it once with yawmul-faṣl (Judgement), between 'For the Day of Judgement' and the first woe. Al-Infiṭār asks it twice with yawmud-dīn (Recompense); the second one opens with thumma instead of wa. Hook: faṣl stays in Al-Mursalāt, which says 'Day of Judgement' again at 77:38; dīn comes as a pair in Al-Infiṭār.

cues.77:14: Al-Mursalāt: yawmul-faṣl, right after 'For the Day of Judgement'; the first woe follows.
cues.82:17: Al-Infiṭār, 1st: wa mā adrāka … yawmud-dīn, after 'never will they be absent'.
cues.82:18: Al-Infiṭār, 2nd: thumma replaces wa; next, no soul can help another.

g2.flow: Ten wayl yawmaʾidhin here, each closing a scene: the Day of Judgement, destroyed peoples, birth from a liquid, earth, mountains and water, the march to what they denied, no speech or excuse, the dare to plot, the righteous rewarded, 'eat a little', refusing to bow. Chant: Day, Nations, Birth, Earth; March, Silence, Plot; Reward, Eat, Bow. The last three sit two ayat apart. Al-Muṭaffifīn has one, after the inscribed register.

cues.77:15: 1st: right after 'what can make you know the Day of Judgement?'
cues.77:19: 2nd: after 'Thus do We deal with the criminals', closing the destroyed former peoples.
cues.77:24: 3rd: after 'excellent are We to determine', closing creation from a disdained liquid.
cues.77:28: 4th: after lofty mountains and sweet water, closing the earth as a container.
cues.77:34: 5th: after 'as if yellowish camels', closing 'proceed to what you used to deny'.
cues.77:37: 6th: after 'nor permitted to make an excuse', closing the Day they will not speak.
cues.77:40: 7th: after 'if you have a plan, plan against Me'; the righteous in shades follow.
cues.77:45: 8th: after 'We thus reward the doers of good', closing fruits and drink.
cues.77:47: 9th: after 'eat and enjoy a little; you are criminals'. Two ayat after the 8th.
cues.77:49: 10th, last: after 'told to bow, they do not bow'; then 'in what statement…?'
cues.83:10: Al-Muṭaffifīn, only once: after 'a register inscribed'; next, who deny the Day of Recompense.

g3.flow: All open inna al-muttaqīna fī, then split. Al-Ḥijr and Adh-Dhāriyāt: jannātin wa ʿuyūn (gardens and springs). Aṭ-Ṭūr: jannātin wa naʿīm (pleasure). Al-Qamar: jannātin wa nahar (rivers). Al-Mursalāt alone has ẓilālin wa ʿuyūn (shades), straight after the seventh woe. Hook in muṣḥaf order: springs, springs, pleasure, rivers, then shades.

cues.15:45: Al-Ḥijr: jannātin wa ʿuyūn, after Hell's seven gates; next, 'Enter it in peace'.
cues.51:15: Adh-Dhāriyāt: jannātin wa ʿuyūn, after 'Taste your torment'.
cues.52:17: Aṭ-Ṭūr: jannātin wa naʿīm (pleasure), after 'burn therein, patient or impatient'.
cues.54:54: Al-Qamar: jannātin wa nahar (rivers), after every small and great thing is inscribed.
cues.77:41: Al-Mursalāt: ẓilālin wa ʿuyūn (shades), straight after the seventh woe; fruits follow.

g4.flow: Same words in both. In Aṭ-Ṭūr it comes after being protected from Hellfire and leads on to reclining on thrones. In Al-Mursalāt it comes after fruits they desire and leads on to 'We thus reward the doers of good', then a woe. Hook: Ṭūr moves on to thrones; Mursalāt moves on to reward, then woe.

cues.52:19: Aṭ-Ṭūr: after protection from Hellfire; next, reclining on thrones lined up.
cues.77:43: Al-Mursalāt: after fruits they desire; next, 'We thus reward the doers of good'.

g5.flow: Aṣ-Ṣāffāt uses innā kadhālika najzil-muḥsinīn three times, each after 'peace upon' a prophet and before 'of Our believing servants': Noah, then Moses and Aaron, then Elias. Al-Mursalāt uses it once, after 'eat and drink in satisfaction', right before the eighth woe. Hook: in Aṣ-Ṣāffāt a greeting of peace comes first; in Al-Mursalāt food comes first.

cues.37:80: Aṣ-Ṣāffāt, 1st: after 'Peace upon Noah among the worlds'.
cues.37:121: Aṣ-Ṣāffāt, 2nd: after 'Peace upon Moses and Aaron'; 'they were' follows.
cues.77:44: Al-Mursalāt: after 'eat and drink in satisfaction'; the eighth woe follows.
